selected: Place the Semantic Firewall before deterministic projection so control-relevant input is typed and closed before current state is derived.

alternatives.reason: Would require model or heuristic semantic judgment for control-relevant conflicts.
Invalid or ambiguous semantics should be rejected before projection rather than projected and diagnosed later.

rationale: This keeps the projector deterministic and makes semantic admissibility a separate fail-closed boundary. The legacy firewall already rejects free-text predicates, unknown decision kinds, and untyped model output for the ten control-decision classes.

research.title: ESAA: Event Sourcing for Autonomous Agents in LLM-Based Software Engineering
research.supports: Structured validated agent intentions separated from deterministic orchestration and projected state.

limitations: Legacy firewall production contracts for every Life control kind are not yet migrated into Build.

selected: Import the legacy contracts/semantic-firewall suite byte-for-byte first, verify provenance, then make only versioned adaptations required by current Build semantics.

alternatives.reason: Would lose tested falsification behavior and provenance.
Old README/workflow/coordination assumptions are stale relative to current Build Merge Queue and source coordination v3.

rationale: The firewall implementation is self-contained and materially richer than a new minimal validator, while surrounding legacy repository mechanisms no longer match current Life.
limitations: Import has not yet occurred in KINETIC-DESIGN-CO/Build.

selected: Use isolated work branches plus component/shared-external-resource claims; ordinary repository paths are integrated by Git conflict detection, required validation, Merge Queue, and merge_group validation rather than exclusive file leases.

alternatives.reason: Adds blocking, expiry, takeover, and cleanup overhead for state Git can safely isolate and Merge Queue can validate.
Git cannot isolate shared external state such as the single Supabase production environment or duplicate component work.

rationale: Move coordination to the semantic/shared-resource layer while leaving source integration to GitHub-native mechanisms. PR #44 implemented this protocol change and passed merge_group and post-merge validation.

research.title: GitHub Merge Queue documentation
research.supports: Native queued latest-base integration with required checks.

limitations: coordination/README.md still describes obsolete repo-file claims and must be reconciled separately.
Terminal claim cleanup and admissions lifecycle are not yet fully automated.

selected: Use a repeatable loop of fresh discovery, typed candidate classification, versioned implementation, falsification, protected integration, live readback, and KEEP/REPLACE/MODIFY/COMBINE/REMOVE reevaluation.

alternatives.reason: Model self-assessment cannot satisfy deterministic verification or control authority.
Misses native capabilities that can delete custom machinery or manual work.

rationale: The system should evolve from current external evidence but only retain changes that survive machine-verifiable tests and live verification.

research.title: ESAA: Event Sourcing for Autonomous Agents in LLM-Based Software Engineering
research.supports: Validated structured events and deterministic orchestration improve traceability and replayability.

research.title: OpenAI connected-app security controls
research.supports: External app actions remain constrained by action controls and safety protections; autonomous workflows need explicit verification boundaries.

limitations: System-evolution policy is not yet bootstrap-required.
No single metric can decide architecture quality; comparisons must use typed requirements and evidence rather than an untyped better/best gate.

selected: Persist frequent evidence-only checkpoints plus a directive ledger and decision-rationale ledger; make checkpoint timing deterministic and bootstrap-required; require fresh live hydration before resuming.

alternatives.reason: Can be lost before creation, omit rationale, and collapse historical observations into current truth.
Not machine-readable repository state and cannot provide durable exact provenance.
Lock branches can change independently; cached ownership becomes stale without the checkpoint changing.

rationale: Capture evidence while work is happening, separate historical observation from live authority, and give future threads enough provenance to reevaluate rather than blindly inherit summaries.

research.title: ESAA: Event Sourcing for Autonomous Agents in LLM-Based Software Engineering
research.supports: Append-only structured events and projected state address long-horizon agent state degradation and provide replay/traceability.

limitations: Checkpoint policy/template/bootstrap integration are not yet merged to main.
The first two recovery checkpoints are summaries and do not contain complete directive provenance.

selected: Project repository-stable current/handoff state deterministically from typed canonical evidence, then hydrate volatile GitHub/Supabase/Vercel facts live before deterministic work selection.

alternatives.reason: Creates multiple authored truth surfaces that can drift.
Lock state changes independently of main.

rationale: Generated repository state removes manual reconciliation drift; fresh live reads preserve currentness for volatile state. The projector should not perform semantic interpretation that belongs in the firewall.

research.title: ESAA: Event Sourcing for Autonomous Agents in LLM-Based Software Engineering
research.supports: Validated append-only events can project deterministic materialized state for autonomous-agent workflows.

limitations: Projector, generated handoff, and live hydration layer are not yet implemented.

selected: Candidate: use narrowly scoped repository-side GitHub App or Actions automation for deterministic housekeeping that the ChatGPT connected-app safety layer may deny, while retaining versioned source, protected CI, and live readback.

alternatives.reason: OpenAI documentation states app permissions do not override safety protections.
Would undermine the safety boundary instead of solving the architectural dependency.

rationale: The GitHub connector can have Contents write permission and still have an action denied by OpenAI safety protections. Repository-side automation could make deterministic housekeeping independent of conversational connector classification, but must be designed with least privilege and no hidden paid dependency.

research.title: Admin controls, security, and compliance for plugins and apps
research.supports: App permission settings do not override safety protections.

research.title: GitHub GITHUB_TOKEN concepts
research.supports: GitHub Actions uses short-lived GitHub App installation access tokens scoped to the repository.

limitations: Proposal is not selected as architecture yet.
A GitHub App may still require additional installation/configuration and exact permission review.

selected: Use a typed engineering goal graph plus an active root-to-leaf goal path. Stable semantic goal identity is separate from execution work, lease, branch, and generation identity. Typed child goals may temporarily become active, but a terminal child returns deterministic selection to its nonterminal parent before unrelated-root work is eligible.

alternatives.reason: Conversation and checkpoints are evidence surfaces and cannot provide one stable machine-readable semantic identity across workers and execution attempts.
GitHub relationships are useful visibility but Issues have zero Life selection/control authority.
It can abandon a nonterminal parent objective after a child operation finishes.

rationale: The parent goal must survive blocker repair, prerequisites, verification, continuity capture, terminal cleanup, defect repair, interruptions, and lease/attempt turnover. Explicit hierarchical state avoids deriving objective continuity from prose or execution identity and lets deterministic selection distinguish a serving child from an unrelated root.

research.title: HIPIF: Hierarchical Planning and Information Folding for Long-Horizon LLM Agents
research.supports: Explicit hierarchical subgoals and folding completed history reduce long-context interference in long-horizon agents.

research.title: TaskWeave: Structure-Aware Long-Horizon Agent Planning
research.supports: Structured hierarchical planning and dependency-aware trace state support long-horizon agent execution.

research.title: Production multi-agent lessons from r/ClaudeCode
research.supports: Community operators report goal drift across chained agent work and use persisted original-goal constraints in handoffs as a mitigation.

limitations: The active auto_issue_dispatch component is owned by another unexpired work item, so parent-first selector integration cannot be mutated by this work yet.
The active Issue #49 problem-intake branch must be reconciled before combined defect-repair lifecycle completion.
The goal graph is not LIVE until protected integration and merged-main readback succeed.
